permutationLabel: Complex: anterior, female, high transsphincteric, obstetric injury
summary: 38-year-old woman with an anterior fistula after two vaginal deliveries (one third-degree tear); probe suggests a high transsphincteric tract. MRI pelvis to map the tract; loose seton / sphincter-preserving repair; no primary fistulotomy.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Recurrent discharge in front of the back passage
inputs.hpi: Two drained abscesses in 18 months; persistent discharge from an opening in front of the anus. Two vaginal deliveries, the second with a third-degree tear; occasional urgency and flatus incontinence already. No IBD symptoms.

exam.other: Perianal: external opening at 1 o’clock, 3 cm from the verge. DRE: reduced squeeze anteriorly; tract felt passing high towards the anorectal ring.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Complex anterior transsphincteric fistula-in-ano
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Complex fistula-in-ano: anterior, female, high transsphincteric, previous obstetric sphincter injury. MRI pelvis; loose seton; sphincter-preserving repair.

mustInclude.note: Complex/anterior fistula in a woman: MRI (or endoanal ultrasound) before any division of sphincter.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano and rectovaginal fistula
guideline.section: Complex fistula (anterior in women, high transsphincteric, pre-existing incontinence): imaging and sphincter-preserving repair; avoid fistulotomy
guideline.citation: Gaertner WB, Burgess PL, Davids JS, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, and rectovaginal fistula. Dis Colon Rectum. 2022;65:964–985.

rationale: Permutation: every complex-fistula feature (anterior, female, high tract, prior obstetric injury, pre-existing incontinence symptoms). A fistulotomy here risks incontinence.
